column3: `0` turns off the deferred pass merging of the TBDR optimizations (which run only with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`)
`=1` keeps the deferred pass merging (with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`) off until the second screenshot has been written, then turns it on, to compare the pictures with and without it
`=<fragment shader key prefix>,…`: those draws compare depth with `ALWAYS`; with `DM_NVN_HILITE`, tells "the depth test rejects every fragment" from "nothing rasterizes"
`=1` fully hashes pool content on every use to find changes the dirty-page tracking missed
`=1` gives every compute dispatch a compute encoder of its own with full barriers, as before (by default dispatches share the copy encoder); `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` does the same
`=1` labels every render encoder `p<pass in frame> <width>x<height> <first 8 digits of the first draw's fragment key> d<draws>` for Instruments traces
`1` runs the replay's Metal encoding on a thread of its own while the submit thread goes on translating; on by default on iOS (`0` turns it off), off on macOS
`0` makes the game's `SyncWait`s wake on the commit feedback handler instead of the GPU's own signal of the fence (on by default)
Which fragment shaders sampling a colour attachment of their own pass read a snapshot of it: `0` none, `all` every shader (slow), `<keys,…>` that list instead of the profile's `feedback_snap`
`0` starts a new GPU texture in a CPU-writable pool as zeros; by default one whose storage the game flushed before its first use is filled from that storage once
`=<N>` prints the NVN call table frame by frame for the first N frames (default 3)
`=1` checks pass merging in the same frame: renders the merged passes again apart and logs the comparison of the attachments every time
`=<f>`, `<f1>-<f2>` or `every:<n>`: logs the GPU start and duration of every encoder of those frames (`[gpuprof]` lines from Metal 4 counter heap timestamps)

column3: `=<fragment key>[,…]` (up to 16) drops all draws of those fragment shaders, to measure their GPU cost or bisect a wrong draw; the picture is wrong
`=<width>` drops all draws whose target width is at most that, to measure the cost of tiny render passes; the picture is wrong
`0` keeps passes into other layers of one array or cube texture level apart (on by default: they run as one layered pass)
`=1` makes `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` also save each target's raw bytes, with a text header line, since converting an HDR target to an 8-bit image truncates
`=<frame>`: `DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE` records copies only from that frame on (default 0)
`=<W>x<H>:<file>`: after each copy into an RGBA16F texture of that size, copies the result into a trace buffer on the GPU timeline; 240 entries are written to the file
`=1` turns on the replay's TBDR pass optimizations (store / load elision, pass merging, same-target continuation); off by default since bindless textures defeat their read inference
`=1` logs non-packaged (non-swizzled) textures in CPU-visible pools
`=<frame>:<path>`, `size=<W>x<H>:<path>` or `layers=<n>:<path>`: saves every colour render target of that frame as PNG (`%d` = serial × 100 + layer × 10 + level)

column3: `=<in-frame pass index>,…`: with `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`, copies those passes' colour attachments as they end and saves them with the end-of-frame dump
`=<n>` logs every registration of texture ID n: what it holds from then on, and the frame being recorded
`=<path>` writes the per-frame NVN call table and timing rows (frame, metric, value) to a TSV, read by `scripts/bench.py`
`0` makes `DM_NVN_TSV` write only the timing rows, without the call counts (about two thirds of the file)

`="name=item,…;…"`: alternating measurement in one run; odd phases of `DM_NVN_UB_N` frames (default 180) take one category in turn (`@set:<global>=<value>` or dropped shader keys) and log present times
`=1` checks every uniform shadow made from memory: the pass ends, the updates land, the replay waits for the GPU and compares (a difference is a red line; slow)
`0` copies uniform shadows of 512 bytes or more on the submit thread, as before (by default a worker copies them)
`0` ends the render pass at every inline uniform update, as before; by default an update inside an open pass is deferred to the pass end and later draws read a shadow (off in TBDR mode)

`=<n>`: the most deferred inline uniform updates kept across a render pass end (default 160); they land before the next copy, a conflicting draw or dispatch, or the submission end; `0` lands them at every pass end
`=<frames>`: the length of each phase of the same-process alternating measurement `DM_NVN_UB` (default 180, minimum 60)
`0`: a uniform block the deferred updates cover only in part ends the pass, as before; by default its shadow starts from memory and takes the submission's queued updates (on by default)
`=1` starts with the DontCare store for unwritten attachments off and turns it on after the second screenshot, for an on/off picture comparison in one run
`0` turns off storing attachments a render pass did not write as DontCare (on by default; part of the TBDR store lookahead), for equivalence comparisons
`0` turns off the cache of resolved vertex stream addresses and vertex argument table writes across draws (on by default), for A/B runs
`=1` scans the indices again at every reuse of a cached vertex conversion range (`vconv_range`) and reports differences
`=1` converts integer vertex inputs fed formats of another class on the CPU, as before, instead of through the shader's shadow inputs (`<key>_bv`)
`0` / `1` overrides the profile's `vconv_range`: CPU vertex conversion only over the vertices each draw reads instead of the whole bound range
Set: logs each NVN memory pool as it is created (address, memory, size, flags) with a backtrace
`=1` turns on the wait ledger: every place a host or game thread waits on the CPU for the GPU or the encode thread, counted per frame
`0` turns off the cross-submission attachment validity ledger, which skips write-backs of colour attachments cleared before their next use (on by default, only with `DM_NVN_TBDR` on)
`=1` logs (`[zb]`) the all-zero blocks per level of each ASTC texture uploaded on the CPU (magenta when drawn); `=<folder>` also writes the raw storage of the first one per format and size
`0` turns off the zero-source skip, which drops a draw whose fragment shader is proven to write 0 over targets already 0 (on by default, only with `DM_NVN_TBDR` on)
Scripted applet state changes at given seconds, `key=value@seconds,…` with keys `focus`, `opmode` and `bg` (`bg=1` / `bg=0` run the whole background round trip), e.g. `bg=1@20,bg=0@25`

column3: `=1` on the Mac merges every controller into player 1, as before, instead of giving each controller a player of its own
`=<bytes>`: the size of the patch area right before the module base for a long text (`BIG_TEXT`); set only by the rewriter's own rerun with the size it needs
`0` / `1` overrides the profile's `core_preempt`: also check already-runnable higher-priority peers on the caller's core after every thread SVC
Set: on the Mac, runs the host's early background loading (`dm_host_preload_start`) as the iOS app does, to exercise that path
`0` makes the display link take the newest queued frame each tick, as before; by default it shows frames in order, at most one tick behind
`=<N>`: the frequency of presentation pacing (default 60); `0` means no frame limit and is for performance profiling only
`display` presents one frame per display-link tick whatever interval the game sets; `game` follows the game's present interval (default: the profile's `present_interval`)
`=<n>` (above 0): the display link's preferred frame latency (default 1)
Present pacing: `0` acquires the drawable itself, `1` (the default) presents on a 60 Hz display link, `2` uses a 120 Hz display link with a frame every other tick
`=<n>`: present snapshots, a ring of n host textures (2 to 4; `1` = 2) the presents are copied to so the game's swapchain texture is free at once; `0` off (default: the profile's `present_snap`)
`metalfx` scales a picture smaller than its rectangle on the screen through MetalFX's spatial scaler; `off` (the default) scales it bilinearly
`=module:offset,…` (Mac only): puts a `brk` at each guest address and on every hit prints the thread, registers, strings they point to and a backtrace, then runs the original instruction

`=e1,e2`: the Switch priority edges of `DM_QOS_MAP` (default `44,59`)
`=1` maps guest thread priority to QoS class: ≤ 44 user-interactive, 45–59 user-initiated, the rest utility (off by default: every guest thread runs user-interactive)
`0.5` to `1.0`: fixes the game's 3D views at that fraction of their size and turns its dynamic resolution off, for builds with a render scale stub; `1.0` (the default) keeps it

column3: `=1` checks every hashed module symbol lookup against a linear search and logs a red line for each mismatch
Apple team ID for the per-game Xcode project, used when `--team-id` / `TEAM_ID` is not given; `build_ipa.sh` uses the placeholder `0000000000` (unsigned) when unset
Temporary storage folder (default `$DM_ROOT/run/platform/temp`); stand-in system data goes in `<DM_TEMP>_sysdata`; the Mac launcher, the iOS app and the NSP script set it
`=write:<n>[:<errno>]` makes the nth save write fail with that errno (default ENOSPC), which refuses the save transaction's commit
`=<point>[:<count>][,…]` makes steps of the save transaction (`mountclone`, `reclone`, `guestname`, `renameback`) fail with ENOSPC
Path of the native `t_geometry` executable; `test_dmsh_geometry.py` runs its native geometry emitter checks only when it is set
`=<n>` creates up to n (at most 512) pthread keys on a thread of its own while the host starts up
`=write:<n>` exits the process (`_exit(9)`) at the nth save write, imitating a kill mid-write
`=1` allocates and keeps a 1 MB shared Metal buffer every 100 ticks: a GPU memory leak on demand
`=<start s>,<duration s>`: counting from the first present, pauses the display link at that point for that long, to check the present fallback
`=1` treats the GPU as one without Metal 4, as on a virtual Mac: the NVN layer starts only its classic part and drops every present
`=<every n>,<ms>[,<in a row>][;…]` sleeps that long before every nth present (and the ones after it in the run): a slow frame on demand
`=<ms>` (with `DM_KBD`) keeps the system keyboard up that long before `DM_KBD`'s text is returned, as a player typing would
`=<ms>` sleeps that long between the keyboard handing back its text and the game's thread getting the result, to check that auto-accept does not act early
`=1` keeps the old upload staging block instead of retiring it, as before the fix, to measure the leak
`=<batch index>` treats that batch of uploads as dropped, to exercise the re-upload path
`0` turns off the thermal cap, which holds the frame step at 30 fps while iOS reports a serious or critical thermal state (on by default)
`=1` logs each SVC (except `SleepThread`) with its first four arguments, and each `CreateThread` with entry, stack, priority and core
`=<tsv path>[,<seconds>]` writes each thread's CPU time (100% = one core) and the total every interval (default 10 s); on iOS a relative path is under `Documents`
`0` turns off the light haptic tap when a touch control is pressed (on by default); launcher setting
`=1` logs each touch-screen read with touch points (sample, finger, position, attributes) and each gesture entry, up to 500 lines
`=1` runs a start-up check of DontCare load and store on private depth-stencil and RGBA8 textures (clear, Load + DontCare, read back) and logs one result line
Folder of the Unreal shader code archives decoded by `uepak.py`, for `shader_split.py` (default `ue_shaders` beside the RomFS); needed when the RomFS has Unreal paks
`=<dir>` (Mac) writes every SPIR-V module the game creates to `<dir>/<key>.spv`; the NSP script's Vulkan shader capture stage sets it
`=1` logs Vulkan object creation in the Vulkan-on-Metal layer
`=<Hz>`: rate at which a host thread fires the vi vsync event when the display link does not drive it (default 60)
`=<s>` dumps all threads after that many seconds (SIGALRM) and turns on the stall watchdog; off unless set
`=<path>` (Mac): when the stall watchdog fires, samples the process for 1 s with `/usr/bin/sample` and writes the thread stacks to that path
`=<s>`: when the frame loop makes no progress for that long (default 15 with `DM_WATCH`), logs a red line, dumps the threads and exits
When set (to any value, `0` included) opens a Mac window with keyboard and controller input; unset runs headless with the guest on the current thread; the Mac launcher sets it
